problems.title: Convert the repeating decimal
problems.question: Evaluate1/3−0.(11)+7/9.
problems.idea: Use exact arithmetic or a simple model of the stated conditions.
steps: Use denominator9:3/9−1/9+7/9=9/9=1.

problems.title: Order repeating decimals and fractions
problems.question: Order A=0.3(12), B=10/33, C=3/11, D=19/55 increasingly.
problems.idea: Use exact arithmetic or a simple model of the stated conditions.
steps: With denominator330, the numerators for A, B, C, D are 103,100,90,114.
Thus C<B<A<D.

problems.title: Count a union of divisor sets
problems.question: A consists of divisors of 81, B of 32. Find |A∪B|.
problems.idea: Use exact arithmetic or a simple model of the stated conditions.
formulas: $|A\cup B|=|A|+|B|-|A\cap B|$.
steps: 81=3⁴ has 5 divisors;32=2⁵ has 6. Their only common positive divisor is 1.
Thus the union contains5+6−1=10 elements.

problems.title: Take the absolute value before the final digit
problems.question: Find the final digit of the absolute value of the negative integer 2024⁸−199¹⁹⁹.
problems.idea: Use exact arithmetic or a simple model of the stated conditions.
formulas: Powers of 4 alternate4,6; odd powers of 9 end in9.
steps: The two powers end in6 and 9. Taking the absolute value reverses the negative difference.
Its final digit is 9−6=3.

problems.title: Enumerate positions on a line
problems.question: Collinear points satisfy AB=10, BC=12, AD=6. Which listed CD length is impossible?
problems.idea: Use exact arithmetic or a simple model of the stated conditions.
formulas: Set A=0, B=10. Then C=22 or −2, and D=6 or −6.
steps: The possible absolute differences |C−D| are 16,28,8,4.
Of the listed lengths 18,4,8,28,16, only 18 is impossible.

problems.title: Apply the operation twice
problems.question: a⊛b is the number of positive divisors of ab. Find(5⊛9)⊛7.
problems.idea: Use exact arithmetic or a simple model of the stated conditions.
formulas: If $n=\prod p_i^{e_i}$, its divisor count is$\prod(e_i+1)$.
steps: 45=3²·5 has 3·2=6 divisors. Thus5⊛9=6.
Now42=2·3·7 has 2³=8 divisors.

problems.title: Remove the common elements
problems.question: A={1,2,4,8}, B={2,4,6,7,9,11}. Find |A△B|.
problems.idea: Use exact arithmetic or a simple model of the stated conditions.
formulas: $A\triangle B=(A\setminus B)\cup(B\setminus A)$.
steps: The common elements2,4 disappear. The remaining elements are 1,8,6,7,9,11, six in all.

problems.title: Account for the one student left over
problems.question: In a class,4/9 are taller than Lika,1/2 shorter, and nobody else has her height. Find the digit sum of the class size.
problems.idea: Use exact arithmetic or a simple model of the stated conditions.
steps: The remaining1/18 of the class is Lika alone. Hence the class has 18 students.
Its digit sum is 1+8=9.
problems.note: The intended fractions must refer to the whole class. If “classmates” is read strictly as excluding Lika, the two fractions fail to account for all classmates.

problems.title: Distance between two midpoints
problems.question: A, B, C, D occur in order with AB=6, BC=7, CD=8. Find the distance between the midpoints of AB and CD.
problems.idea: Use exact arithmetic or a simple model of the stated conditions.
formulas: The distance is AB/2+BC+CD/2.

problems.title: Supplementary angles in a ratio
problems.question: Two adjacent supplementary angles are in ratio2:3. Find their difference.
problems.idea: Use exact arithmetic or a simple model of the stated conditions.
formulas: The angles sum to 180°, so five equal parts total180°.
steps: One part is 36°. The angles are 72° and 108°, whose difference is 36°.

problems.title: A product divisible by a chain of factors
problems.question: Distinct positive integers satisfy ab=c, d=a/3, b=5e,2f=d. Which number is divisible by the other five?
problems.idea: Use exact arithmetic or a simple model of the stated conditions.
formulas: $a=3d=6f$ and $b=5e$, so $c=ab$.
steps: The product c is divisible by a and b. Because d and f divide a, and e divides b, they also divide c.
Thus c is divisible by all five other numbers.

problems.title: The empty set is always a subset
problems.question: Which displayed expression is always a subset of A?
problems.idea: Use exact arithmetic or a simple model of the stated conditions.
formulas: $A\setminus(A\cup B\cup C)=\varnothing$.
steps: Every element of A already belongs to the union, so none survives the subtraction.
The empty set is a subset of every set. The other displayed expressions can retain elements outside A.

problems.title: First trisection point on a number line
problems.question: A, C, D, B occur in order with AC=CD=DB. A has coordinatea, B coordinateb. Find C.
problems.idea: Use exact arithmetic or a simple model of the stated conditions.
formulas: Each step is(b−a)/3.

problems.title: A class size divisible by three denominators
problems.question: Fractions1/3,1/4,1/7 of the Grade7 students receive specified grades. Their number equals a line angle in degrees. Find the number.
problems.idea: Use exact arithmetic or a simple model of the stated conditions.
formulas: The class size is a positive multiple of lcm(3,4,7)=84. A smaller line angle is at most90°.
steps: The only positive multiple of 84 no larger than 90 is 84.

problems.title: Bisectors halve supplementary angles
problems.question: Bisectors of same-side interior angles between parallel lines make acute anglesα,β with the parallels. Their difference is 20°. Find the smaller.
problems.idea: Use exact arithmetic or a simple model of the stated conditions.
formulas: The original angles sum to 180°, soα+β=90°.
steps: Solveα+β=90 andβ−α=20. Adding gives 2β=110, soβ=55 andα=35.

problems.title: Nested subtraction alternates signs
problems.question: Evaluate1−(2−(3−(4−(5−(6−7))))).
problems.idea: Use exact arithmetic or a simple model of the stated conditions.
formulas: Removing successive parentheses gives 1−2+3−4+5−6+7.
steps: Pair the first six terms:(1−2)+(3−4)+(5−6)+7=−3+7=4.

problems.title: Two analog clocks must both wrap by twelve hours
problems.question: One clock loses15 min/day, another gains10 min/day. Both are correct at noon. Which listed day count makes both correct again?
problems.idea: Use exact arithmetic or a simple model of the stated conditions.
formulas: An analog dial repeats after720 min. Require15d and 10d to be multiples of 720.
steps: Thus d must be a multiple of 48 and 72. Their least common multiple is 144.
144 is the listed simultaneous return time.
problems.note: This uses ordinary 12-hour analog dials. Distinguishing morning from evening would instead require a 24-hour return.

problems.title: Greatest fixed divisor of a consecutive product
problems.question: Find the greatest integer dividing6n(n+1)(n+2) for every positive integern.
problems.idea: Use exact arithmetic or a simple model of the stated conditions.
formulas: Among three consecutive integers, one is divisible by 3 and one by 2. Thus n(n+1)(n+2) is divisible by 6.
steps: The whole expression is always divisible by 36. At n=1, it is exactly 36, so no larger fixed divisor is possible.

problems.title: No parallel-line assumption is given
problems.question: Two arbitrary lines are cut by a transversal. Which of the listed equal-angle or special-sum assertions must hold?
problems.idea: Use exact arithmetic or a simple model of the stated conditions.
formulas: At an ordinary crossing, only vertical equality and supplementary adjacent sums are guaranteed. Parallel-line angle relations need parallelism.
steps: For example, use acute crossing angles30° and 50°. The eight angles are two copies each of 30°,150°,50°,130°.
No three are equal, no pair sums to 120°, and the claimed parallel-line interior relations fail. Thus none of the listed assertions is necessary.

problems.title: Three lines create three repeated angle sizes
problems.question: Three distinct lines meet at a point. Three of the six angles are in ratio2:3:4. Find largest minus smallest.
problems.idea: Use exact arithmetic or a simple model of the stated conditions.
formulas: Opposite angles are equal, so the three different sizes sum to 180°.
steps: Write them2t,3t,4t. Then9t=180°, giving t=20°.
Largest minus smallest=(4−2)t=40°.

problems.title: Subsets of a prime-divisor set
problems.question: How many subsets has the set of prime divisors of 420?
problems.idea: Use exact arithmetic or a simple model of the stated conditions.
formulas: $420=2^2\cdot3\cdot5\cdot7$. A set of k elements has 2^k subsets.
steps: There are four distinct primes, so 2⁴=16 subsets, including the empty set.

problems.title: A visible factor already contains nine
problems.question: Find the remainder of 17·48·(9n+4)·(18m+7)·(23k+2)·(45p+18) modulo9.
problems.idea: Use exact arithmetic or a simple model of the stated conditions.
steps: This factor is a multiple of 9, so the entire integer product is divisible by 9.

problems.title: Use opposite signs to simplify absolute values
problems.question: A, B, C have increasing coordinates|a|,|b|,|a−b|. D=|a+b|, M=|a|/3, N=|b|/7. Which listed order is impossible?
problems.idea: Use exact arithmetic or a simple model of the stated conditions.
formulas: Put p=|a|, q=|b|. The strict order forces opposite signs and 0<p<q, so C=p+q, D=q−p.
steps: Because D=q−p<q=B, the proposed order III, which places B before D, is impossible.
OrdersI, II, IV are attainable with(p, q)=(3,8),(1,8),(14,15), respectively. Each pair can be realised by a=p, b=−q.

problems.title: Maximise triangles on two parallel lines
problems.question: Eight marked points lie on two parallel lines. What is the maximum number of triangles with marked vertices?
problems.idea: Use exact arithmetic or a simple model of the stated conditions.
formulas: If one line hask points, the count is C(k,2)(8−k)+kC(8−k,2)=3k(8−k).
steps: This quadratic is largest at k=4. Then the count is 3·4·4=48.
Every triangle uses two points on one line and one on the other, so none is omitted.

problems.title: Two successive angle bisectors
problems.question: An angle bisector meets a line parallel to one side; the bisector of the new angle makes20° with that side. Which listed original angle is possible?
problems.idea: Use exact arithmetic or a simple model of the stated conditions.
formulas: If the original angle isθ∈(0°,180°), the first bisector makesθ/2 with the parallel; the second can makeθ/4 or 90°−θ/4.
steps: Settingθ/4=20° givesθ=80°. The alternative90°−θ/4=20° would giveθ=280°, outside the ordinary angle range.
